sections.subtitle: 2-4 Weeks Timeline
sections.description: Comprehensive sponsorship oversight for skilled and unskilled labor.

steps.title: Quota & Offer Letter
steps.description: Verify visa quota availability and issue MoHRE-standard offer letter to the candidate.

steps.title: Entry Permit (Pink Slip)
steps.description: Apply for the preliminary entry permit to allow the employee to enter the UAE legally.

steps.title: Change of Status

steps.title: Medical & Biometrics

steps.title: Contract Attestation

steps.title: Visa Stamping/E-Visa

sections.title: Employment Regulations 2026
sections.subtitle: Statutory Compliance
sections.description: Critical updates for headcount management and hiring targets.

items.title: Emiratisation (Nafis)
items.text: Mainland firms with 20-49 staff must hire 1 Emirati by end-2025 and an additional 1 by end-2026. Non-compliance results in monthly fines of AED 6,000+ per headcount.

items.title: Fixed-Term Contracts
items.text: All private sector employees must be on fixed-term contracts (max 3 years, renewable). Unlimited contracts are no longer valid under the 2022 Labor Law.

items.title: Golden Visa Eligibility
items.text: Highly skilled professionals with a monthly basic salary of AED 30,000+ can apply for self-sponsored 10-year residency, reducing EOR dependency.

items.title: Part-Time & Remote
items.text: Specific MOHRE work permits are required for part-time, temporary, or flexible work arrangements to avoid labor inspection fines.

sections.title: Mandatory Benefits
sections.subtitle: Legal Requirements
sections.description: Statutory entitlements for all employees under UAE labor law.

items.title: Health Insurance
items.text: Mandatory for all employees. In Dubai (ISAHD) and Abu Dhabi (CHIAD), the employer MUST provide a minimum level of coverage (Essential Benefit Plan).

items.title: Annual Leave
items.text: 30 calendar days for each year of service. 2 days per month if employed more than 6 months but less than a year.

items.title: Unemployment Insurance
items.text: ILOE (Involuntary Loss of Employment) is mandatory for ALL employees. While typically paid by the employee, the EOR must ensure registration.

items.title: Sick Leave
items.text: Entitled to 90 days total (after probation): first 15 days full pay, next 30 days half pay, remaining 45 days unpaid.

sections.title: The Monthly WPS Cycle
sections.subtitle: Deadlines & SIF Format
sections.description: The standardized process for salary disbursement enforced by MoHRE.

steps.title: Data Consolidation
steps.description: Gather basic pay, housing, transport, and variable commissions for all staff.

steps.title: SIF File Generation
steps.description: Create the Salary Information File (.SIF) containing Employer ID and Bank Agent ID.

steps.title: Portal Submission
steps.description: Upload the SIF to the bank's WPS portal. Common bank fees range from AED 50 to AED 100 per file.

steps.title: Central Bank Validation
steps.description: The UAE Central Bank validates the file against registered MoHRE contracts.

steps.title: Fund Release
steps.description: Salaries are credited to employee accounts or exchange house cards (e.g., Al Ansari).

sections.title: WPS Compliance Rules
sections.subtitle: Avoiding Blocks & Fines
sections.description: Strict thresholds for maintaining a healthy company status.

items.title: The 80% Rule
items.text: At least 80% of the total registered workforce must receive their salary via WPS every month to avoid labor system blocks.

items.title: Payment Deadlines
items.text: Salaries are considered late if not paid within 15 days of the due date. Delays beyond 30 days trigger immediate work permit bans.

items.title: SIF Record Fees
items.text: Banks typically charge AED 3.15 per employee record in the SIF file. Manual branch processing is significantly more expensive (AED 700+).

items.title: Unpaid Leave Documentation
items.text: Employees on unpaid leave must be reported via the MoHRE portal to prevent 'salary mismatch' flags during SIF validation.

sections.title: End of Service Gratuity
sections.subtitle: Statutory Calculation
sections.description: Mandatory benefit for expatriates upon contract termination.

items.title: Statutory Formula
items.text: 21 days of basic wage for each year (yrs 1-5). 30 days of basic wage for each year thereafter (yrs 5+).

items.title: Eligibility Threshold
items.text: Gratuity is only payable after 1 continuous year of service. Probation periods are included in the cumulative calculation.

items.title: Global Pension (GP)
items.text: DIFC-based firms use the DEWS (DIFC Employee Workplace Savings) scheme instead of end-of-service gratuity.

items.title: Maximum Entitlement
items.text: The total gratuity payment cannot exceed two years' worth of the employee's total wages.

sections.title: Social Security (GPSSA)
sections.subtitle: UAE & GCC Citizens
sections.description: Mandatory pension contributions for local talent.

items.title: Registration Deadline
items.text: Emirati staff must be registered with the General Pension and Social Security Authority (GPSSA) within 30 days of joining.

items.title: Contribution Split 2026
items.text: Employer share is 12.5% to 15%, employee share is 5%. Calculations are based on Basic salary + specific allowances.

items.title: GCC Reciprocity
items.text: Omani, Saudi, and Kuwaiti nationals in UAE must be enrolled in their home country's pension scheme via the GPSSA portal.

sections.title: Year-End Compliance
sections.subtitle: Annual Audit Prep
sections.description: Critical tasks to close the financial year for UAE payroll.

steps.title: Gratuity Reconciliation
steps.description: Verify EOS accruals against current basic salaries and tenure updates.

steps.title: SIF Audit
steps.description: Cross-reference annual bank disbursements with MoHRE registered figures.

steps.title: Pension Adjustment
steps.description: Update GPSSA contributions based on annual salary increments for Emirati staff.

steps.title: Leave Entitlement Carryover
steps.description: Calculate and document unused annual leave for the next cycle per labor law.

heroData.title: UAE Company Formation
heroData.subtitle: Mainland & 40+ Free Zones
heroData.description: Navigate the complexities of UAE entity setup. From 100% foreign-owned Mainland companies to specialized Free Zones like DMCC, ADGM, and DIFC, we handle the entire licensing and registration workflow.
heroData.bestFor: Enterprises and tech startups establishing a physical presence in the MEA region.

sections.title: Formation Roadmap
sections.subtitle: 5-15 Days Timeline
sections.description: Standard procedure for establishing a legal entity in the UAE.

steps.title: Jurisdiction Choice
steps.description: Select between Mainland (DED), Free Zone (e.g., DMCC), or Offshore (e.g., JAFZA).

steps.title: Activity Selection
steps.description: Map your business to specific MoHRE and DED activity codes (e.g., 'IT Consultancy').

steps.title: Trade Name Approval
steps.description: Reserve a unique name. Note: Names with 'Global' or 'International' carry higher reservation fees.

steps.title: Initial Approval
steps.description: Obtain a 'No Objection' certificate from relevant authorities to proceed with leasing.

steps.title: Office Lease (Ejari)
steps.description: Sign a physical or virtual office lease. Mandatory for license issuance in most jurisdictions.

steps.title: License Issuance
steps.description: Pay final fees and receive your Commercial, Industrial, or Professional license.

sections.title: Ownership & Control
sections.subtitle: 100% Foreign Ownership
sections.description: Understanding the 2021 Commercial Companies Law changes.

items.title: Mainland Liberalization
items.text: Non-oil commercial activities in the Mainland no longer require a local Emirati partner (51%). Investors can own 100% of the company.

items.title: Strategic Impact List
items.text: Certain sectors (Defense, Telecom, Banking) still require Emirati majority ownership or UAE Cabinet approval.

items.title: Local Service Agent
items.text: Professional licenses (e.g., Doctors, Lawyers) still require a Local Service Agent (LSA) for MoHRE liaison, though ownership remains 100% foreign.

sections.title: Corporate Banking
sections.subtitle: Final Compliance Gate
sections.description: The most complex step in the UAE setup journey.

items.title: KYC Depth
items.text: Banks like Wio, EDB, and FAB require 3-6 months of personal/business bank statements and proof of residency for all UBOs.

items.title: Digital Banking
items.text: Wio and Mashreq NeoBiz offer faster onboarding (sub-48 hours) for SMEs compared to traditional branch-based banking (4-6 weeks).

items.title: Sanction Checks
items.text: Strict screening for transactions involving high-risk jurisdictions. Maintaining a clean audit trail is vital for account longevity.

sections.title: License Renewal Obligations
sections.subtitle: Annual Maintenance
sections.description: Maintaining legal standing for your UAE entity.

items.title: Grace Periods
items.text: Most jurisdictions offer a 30-day grace period. Beyond this, daily fines of AED 100 - 500 apply, and the license may be suspended.

items.title: Ejari Sync
items.text: License renewal requires a valid office lease (Ejari). Virtual offices in Free Zones must also show active renewal status.

items.title: Audit Submission
items.text: Ensure audited financials (if required) are uploaded to the DED/Free Zone portal at least 30 days before the license expiry.

steps.title: Intermediation License

steps.title: Temporary Staffing

sections.title: Emiratisation Sourcing
sections.subtitle: Meeting Nafis Targets
sections.description: Strategy for hiring UAE National citizens.

items.title: Salary Minima
items.text: Effective Jan 2026, the minimum monthly wage for Emiratis in the private sector is AED 6,000 for university graduates.

items.title: Nafis Platform
items.text: All vacancies for UAE nationals MUST be posted on the Nafis portal for at least 5 days before an offer can be finalized.

items.title: Pension Support
items.text: Nafis provides pension contribution support (up to AED 1,250/month) for eligible Emirati employees, reducing the employer's burden.

sections.title: Candidate Protections
sections.subtitle: Ethical Recruitment
sections.description: Strict MoHRE rules protecting foreign workers.

items.title: No Placement Fees
items.text: It is ILLEGAL in the UAE to charge candidates any fees for recruitment. All costs must be borne by the employer.

items.title: Passport Retention
items.text: Employers and agencies are strictly prohibited from retaining an employee's original passport.

items.title: Offer Letter Integrity
items.text: The terms in the MoHRE-approved offer letter cannot be changed to the candidate's detriment in the final labor contract.

sections.title: Security & Privacy
sections.subtitle: UAE Data Law Compliance
sections.description: Protecting sensitive HR data under local regulations.

items.title: Personal Data Law
items.text: Compliance with Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 regarding the Protection of Personal Data is mandatory for HR vendors.

items.title: Local Hosting
items.text: Many government-linked entities require HR data to be hosted on UAE-based servers (e.g., Azure UAE or AWS ME).

items.title: SOC2/ISO27001
items.text: Ensure your HRIS provider maintains high international security standards for cloud-based payroll records.

sections.title: Cloud Security Framework
sections.subtitle: Data Protection
sections.description: Technical standards for UAE HR software vendors.

items.title: Encryption At Rest
items.text: All employee PII (Personally Identifiable Information) must be encrypted using AES-256 standards as per TDRA recommendations.

items.title: Access Logging
items.text: Maintain immutable audit logs for all administrative actions, required for FTA and MoHRE compliance reviews.

items.title: MFA Mandate
items.text: Enable Multi-Factor Authentication for all 'Manager' and 'Admin' level roles to prevent unauthorized payroll manipulation.
